source_text: Illud tamen nequaquam inficiari possumus, quod plurimum, ut dixi, turbis placeat, luteis tamen delicta voluntatis imputare naturae, et infamatione seminum morum petulantiam vindicare; ut numquam quis emendare conetur, quod sperat in se ipso alterum perpetrare.
pass_a_gloss: That, however, we can in no way deny, that it pleases the crowds very much, as I have said, yet filthy ones, to impute the offenses of the will to nature, and by a slander of seeds to vindicate the wantonness of manners; so that no one ever tries to amend what he hopes another thing in himself is perpetrating.

lemmas.lexica: LS semen; Blaise bodily seed vs transmitted sin
LS delictum; Blaise Rom 5 delictum vs donum
LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will

pass_b_english: Yet we certainly cannot deny what I have said: filthy crowds greatly enjoy blaming nature for the offenses of the will and defending moral wantonness by slandering human seed. The result is that no one tries to correct what he expects something else within him to be committing.

choices.why: Bodily seed of generation; Julian denies it carries a will's sin.
Paul's delictum of the one man; an act, not a nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
